newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament votes in new government.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament votes in new government.

text.p: Slovenia's parliament approved a new government headed by centre-left Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Thursday, ending almost three months of political uncertainty in the ex-Yugoslav republic.
"I congratulate all newly elected ministers," parliamentary president Janez Podobnik told the assembly after the secret ballot. The vote was 52 to 37 in favour of Drnovsek's cabinet line-up.
The government, formed over three months after an inconclusive November general election, is the third since Slovenia gained independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991.
Drnovsek of the Liberal Democrats forged a coalition with the conservative People's Party and the pensioners' party Desus to secure at least 49 votes in the 90-seat assembly.
The Liberal Democrats and the People's Party each have nine ministers in his cabinet, while Desus has one.
"We got as many votes as we expected. I think this should be a solid enough support for the government," Drnovsek said after the vote.
His first attempt to form a government in coalition with the United List of Social Democrats, the Nationalist Party and Desus was rejected by parliament three weeks ago by an even vote of 45 to 45.

Drnovsek said the government's first tasks would include drawing up a budget for the current year, wrapping up the country's mass privatisation programme and stepping up its efforts to join the European Union.

"The government is balanced...and will try to accomplish basic strategic goals like membership of European organisations and NATO, improved economic competitiveness and a balanced development of Slovenia," he said.
Dronvsek has been acting prime minister since April 1992.
